title: Before you begin
line: The whole story in six sessions: a map for everything after.
why: Walk the whole cathedral once, quickly, before you go hall by hall.

title: The Bible
label: The Bible
line: Jerusalem: the story everything else rests on.
why: Every other hall assumes you know this story. It is the way in, at the west door.

later.title: Exodus and the law
later.question: What are freedom and law for?
texts: Maimonides, Guide for the Perplexed III (Friedländer)

later.title: Kings and prophets
later.question: What happens when power forgets justice?
voices: the archaeology of David (the Tel Dan inscription)

later.title: Psalms and wisdom
later.question: How do we pray, think and live in God's world?

later.title: The Sermon on the Mount
later.question: What did Jesus teach about how to live?
texts: Augustine, Our Lord's Sermon on the Mount
Tolstoy, The Kingdom of God Is Within You (Garnett)

later.title: The last week and the cross
later.question: What happened in Jerusalem, and why does it matter?

later.title: The first Christians
later.question: How did a few followers of a crucified man change an empire?

later.title: The end of the story
later.question: Where is history going?

title: Athens
label: Athens
line: The Greeks: reason, the soul and the good life.
why: The second root of the West. Jerusalem gave it a story; Athens gave it questions and the tools to answer them.

later.title: Homer and the heroes
later.question: What did the Greeks think a great life was?

later.title: Tragedy
later.question: Can suffering teach us?
texts: Sophocles, Oedipus the King and Antigone (Jebb)

later.title: Democracy and its dangers
later.question: Who should rule, and how?

later.title: The first historians
later.question: How did history begin, and what does power do?
texts: Thucydides, the plague and the Melian dialogue (Crawley)

later.title: Number and nature
later.question: How did the Greeks begin to explain the world?

later.title: Socrates
later.question: What is the examined life?

later.title: Plato
later.question: What is real, and what is the soul?

later.title: Aristotle
later.question: What is a thing for, and what is a person for?
later.note: Faces Aristotle's defence of 'natural slaves' honestly.

later.title: Epicureans and Stoics
later.question: How do you find peace?

title: Rome and the First Church
label: Rome and the
First Church
line: Where Athens met Jerusalem, and an empire was changed.
why: Rome gave the West its law and order; the first Christians changed what it valued.

later.title: Rome: Cicero, Virgil and the law
later.question: What did Rome give us?
texts: Cicero, On Duties and the Dream of Scipio

later.title: When Athens met Jerusalem
later.question: Can philosophy and faith meet?

later.title: The martyrs and the empire
later.question: Why did Rome persecute Christians, and how did it end?

later.title: Augustine
later.question: Why are we restless, and what are the two cities?

later.title: The fall of Rome and what survived
later.question: What survives when a civilisation falls?

title: What Christians Believe
label: What Christians
Believe
line: At the crossing, under the cross: the questions at the centre of everything.
why: Every hall opens from here. These are the beliefs that held the West together, and the hardest questions put to them.

later.title: Who God is: the Creed
later.question: What does the Creed say, and why?

later.title: Why the cross?
later.question: How can one death save?

later.title: Did Jesus rise?
later.question: Did the resurrection happen?
voices: N. T. Wright and his critics

later.title: The line through the heart
later.question: Where does evil come from?

later.title: Job
later.question: What does God owe the innocent?

later.title: One way among many?
later.question: How should Christians see other faiths?
texts: Nicholas of Cusa, On the Peace of Faith

title: Christendom
label: Christendom
why: Monasteries, universities, cathedrals, law and chivalry: the medieval West, its glories and its failures.

later.title: Monks who saved the West
later.question: How did learning survive?

later.title: Reason and revelation
later.question: Can faith and reason agree?

later.title: Cathedrals and universities
later.question: How did the Middle Ages build its schools?
texts: Abelard, The Story of My Misfortunes

later.title: Chivalry: the making of a knight
later.question: What is strength for?
texts: Ramon Llull, The Book of the Order of Chivalry (Caxton)

later.title: The Crusades: what really happened?
later.question: Holy war, or a betrayal of Christ?
texts: Fulcher of Chartres on Urban II at Clermont
later.note: Faced honestly: the hall's case against.

later.title: The rule of law
later.question: Why should even kings be under the law?

later.title: Dante
later.question: Where does the road through hell lead?

later.title: The mystics
later.question: Can God be known, not only known about?

title: Reformation and New Science
label: Reformation
and New
Science
line: 1500–1700: a broken church, a new world, a new science.
why: The age that tore Christendom apart and, out of the wreckage, found religious freedom, human rights and modern science.

later.title: The Reformation
later.question: What was it about, and what did it cost?
texts: Luther, The Freedom of a Christian

later.title: The King James Bible
later.question: How did one translation shape English?
texts: the King James Bible (1611) and 'The Translators to the Reader'

later.title: The New World and the rights of man
later.question: Are all peoples equal before God?
texts: Francisco de Vitoria, On the Indians
later.note: Where universal rights and international law began, as a Christian protest against conquest.

later.question: How did Christians learn to live with difference?

later.title: Shakespeare
later.question: What do the plays know about mercy and grace?

later.title: The poets
later.question: What can poetry say about God?

later.title: Faith and the new science
later.question: Did science and faith go to war?
texts: Galileo, Letter to the Grand Duchess Christina

later.title: Pascal and doubt
later.question: Is it reasonable to bet on God?

title: The Modern Age
label: The Modern
Age
line: 1700 to today: freedom, its triumphs and its catastrophes.
why: Rights, science, the end of slavery, the death of God and the century of the camps, and what the West must remember to survive.

later.title: Rights and revolutions
later.question: Where do our rights come from?

later.title: The end of slavery
later.question: Why did abolition begin in the Christian West?

later.title: Scotland's Enlightenment
later.question: What did Edinburgh teach the modern world?
texts: Adam Smith, The Theory of Moral Sentiments and The Wealth of Nations

later.title: Hume and the miracles
later.question: Can a reasonable person believe in miracles?
texts: George Campbell, A Dissertation on Miracles (1762)

later.title: Darwin and design
later.question: Does evolution leave room for God?

later.title: The death of God?
later.question: What happens to a world that stops believing?

later.title: Dostoevsky
later.question: If there is no God, is everything permitted?

later.title: The twentieth century: what went wrong?
later.question: What happens when the West abandons its foundations?

later.title: After the death of God
later.question: How did Christians answer the twentieth century?

later.title: The world church
later.question: What does Christianity look like beyond Europe?

later.title: In defence of the West
later.question: What is the West, and is it worth defending?
texts: Solzhenitsyn's Harvard address (1978), in our own words
later.note: The capstone: what the West is, its crimes judged by its own principles, the strongest critiques and the answers.

title: The Good Life
label: The Good
Life
line: Everything learned, lived: virtue, love and nobility.
why: Knowing the West is not enough. This hall is about becoming the kind of person it was meant to form.

later.title: The four virtues
later.question: What are courage, justice, self-control and wisdom?

later.title: Faith, hope and love
later.question: What are the virtues that look beyond us?

later.title: The seven deadly sins
later.question: What quietly shapes us?

later.title: Honour, duty and service
later.question: What does a noble life look like today?
texts: Newman, The Idea of a University (the gentleman)

later.title: The art of persuasion
later.question: How do you defend what is true and good?
texts: Lincoln, the Gettysburg Address and Second Inaugural

later.title: Love, friendship and marriage

voices: C. S. Lewis, The Four Loves
later.note: Sets out the traditions on sexuality fairly; needs a pastor's review.

later.title: Work and money
later.question: Is work holy, and how much is enough?

later.title: Guilt and forgiveness
later.question: Can we be forgiven, and can we forgive?

title: Prayer
label: Prayer
line: At the altar: where it all leads.
why: The cathedral was built for this. Everything else in Rose Window comes to rest here.

later.title: How to read the Bible
later.question: How do you read a text so that it reads you?
texts: Guigo II, The Ladder of Monks

later.title: What happens at church
later.question: Why do Christians baptise and break bread?

later.title: Holy places and holy time
later.question: Why do people set places and times apart?

later.title: Finding God's will

texts: Ignatius of Loyola, rules for discernment
